russia-criminal-case.title: Russian criminal case and domestic defence record
russia-criminal-case.subtitle: This part of the archive follows what happened inside Russia after the case was opened: complaints, replies, refusals, and repeated attempts to obtain a real review on the merits.

investigator-complaints.title: Complaints about investigators: Kuznetsov and Chugunkov
investigator-complaints.subtitle: A focused record of complaints about investigative inaction and the stock replies that followed.
investigator-complaints.contains: The outgoing complaints, supporting appendices, replies from Kuznetsov and Chugunkov, and the prosecutor’s reactions to those filings.
investigator-complaints.proves: That the investigative side kept answering formally without addressing the substance of the complaints.
investigator-complaints.purpose: To show the repeating pattern of non-response at the investigative level.

prosecutor-complaints.title: Complaints about prosecutors: Mitrokhina and Prokopenko
prosecutor-complaints.subtitle: The supervision track inside the prosecution service and the attempts to challenge superficial prosecutorial replies.
prosecutor-complaints.contains: Registration notices, replies signed by Mitrokhina and Prokopenko, complaints to the General Prosecutor’s Office, and compiled bundles of replies.
prosecutor-complaints.proves: That even the supervisory layer never moved to a substantive review and stayed within a bureaucratic paper exchange.
prosecutor-complaints.purpose: To document the failure of prosecutorial oversight as an effective remedy.

termination-and-fabrication.title: Requests to terminate the case and allegations of fabrication
termination-and-fabrication.subtitle: This block gathers the filings where the defence directly argued that the criminal case should be dropped and that the evidentiary narrative had been fabricated.
termination-and-fabrication.contains: Requests to terminate the case, complaints about fabrication, filings on international legal assistance, and related confirmations.
termination-and-fabrication.proves: That the defence raised the absence of any crime and the artificial nature of the criminal narrative clearly and in time.
termination-and-fabrication.purpose: To collect the core merits position in one place.

state-petitions-and-upch.title: President, Federation Council, and Ombudsman track
state-petitions-and-upch.subtitle: Petitions to Russia’s senior state bodies and human-rights institutions.
state-petitions-and-upch.contains: Petitions, registration notices, and replies from the presidential administration, the Federation Council, and the federal ombudsman’s office.
state-petitions-and-upch.proves: That the issue was raised not only with investigators and prosecutors but also at the highest institutional level inside Russia.
state-petitions-and-upch.purpose: To show the breadth of domestic efforts made before turning outward.

russia-criminal-case.contains: Complaints against investigators and prosecutors, crime reports, petitions to the FSB and senior state bodies, and court papers tied to access-to-justice issues.
russia-criminal-case.proves: That the defence did not avoid Russian procedures: it used them repeatedly and mostly encountered forwarding letters, template replies, and procedural refusals.
russia-criminal-case.purpose: To give readers the full Russian procedural background before the extradition and international chapters begin.

crime-reports.title: Crime reports
crime-reports.subtitle: A separate line of filings reporting alleged offences linked to the investigation, witnesses, and procedural actions in the case.
crime-reports.contains: Crime reports concerning Salikov, filings about false testimony, the submission to the Investigative Committee, and the related KUSP materials.
crime-reports.proves: That the defence framed the misconduct not only as a procedural grievance but also as separate reportable offences requiring investigation.
crime-reports.purpose: To show the attempt to trigger a full criminal-law review of the alleged abuse.

fsb-and-security-track.title: FSB and security-agency track
fsb-and-security-track.subtitle: A separate paper trail of submissions to the FSB and the responses that mostly amounted to registration or forwarding.
fsb-and-security-track.contains: FSB submissions, correspondence concerning Salikov and Palkin, ombudsman-routing replies, and forwarding notices.
fsb-and-security-track.proves: That even allegations involving corruption links and organised criminal influence led to bureaucratic circulation rather than a substantive check.
fsb-and-security-track.purpose: To document how the security and control track was exhausted without a real result.

court-challenges-search-and-seizure.title: Court challenges to the wanted status and related measures
court-challenges-search-and-seizure.subtitle: Court materials dealing with the wanted listing and the procedural steps built around it.
court-challenges-search-and-seizure.contains: The Article 125 complaint, the court order refusing the search-related application, and the Moscow City Court reply tied to the wanted status.
court-challenges-search-and-seizure.proves: That the wanted designation itself became a procedural shield against any real judicial review.
court-challenges-search-and-seizure.purpose: To isolate the part of the case where search-related measures turned into a barrier to justice.

court-access-refusals.title: Court refusals and blocked access to review
court-access-refusals.subtitle: The paper trail of returns, refusals to accept complaints, and refusals to move the case any further.
court-access-refusals.contains: Replies from Tverskoy Court and Moscow City Court, refusals to accept complaints, the return order under Article 125, and the cassation refusal.
court-access-refusals.proves: That merits complaints were routinely filtered out before they could be heard in court.
court-access-refusals.purpose: To document denial of effective access to justice as a standalone issue.

related-criminal-judgments.title: Related judgments in other criminal proceedings
related-criminal-judgments.subtitle: Judicial acts concerning other defendants that investigators later cited by analogy.
related-criminal-judgments.contains: The conviction of other defendants and the appeal ruling in that related criminal storyline.
related-criminal-judgments.proves: That outside judgments were used as background and supposed prejudice, even though they do not replace a merits review in Lagovskii’s own case.
related-criminal-judgments.purpose: To separate contextual criminal judgments from the documents directly concerning Lagovskii.

extradition-serbia.title: Extradition proceedings in Serbia
extradition-serbia.subtitle: The Serbian chapter is organised as one continuous process: from the Russian request to the Serbian court rulings and the parallel advocacy work.

extradition-request-and-charge.title: Extradition request and charge narrative
extradition-request-and-charge.subtitle: The opening package of the extradition case: the official Russian request and the accusatory narrative used to support it.
extradition-request-and-charge.contains: The Prosecutor General’s extradition request, the formal charge, and the defence’s detailed critique of errors and contradictions in that text.
extradition-request-and-charge.proves: That the foundation of the extradition request is itself factually disputed, internally uneven, and at odds with the arbitration record.
extradition-request-and-charge.purpose: To show where the Serbian case begins and why the defence contests its starting premise.

search-arrest-and-red-notice.title: Wanted status, arrest, and Red Notice basis
search-arrest-and-red-notice.subtitle: The procedural acts that pushed the case from a Russian file into the international sphere.
search-arrest-and-red-notice.contains: Orders on the domestic search, international search, and in absentia arrest, including the versions used in the Serbian file.
search-arrest-and-red-notice.proves: That the international track grew out of measures adopted without a full adversarial process.
search-arrest-and-red-notice.purpose: To set out the legal backbone of the cross-border phase of the case.

serbian-court-decisions.title: Serbian court decisions
serbian-court-decisions.subtitle: The main judicial decisions issued in Serbia on the extradition request.
serbian-court-decisions.contains: Appeal materials and rulings from the higher Serbian courts dealing with surrender.
serbian-court-decisions.proves: How Serbian courts treated the Russian file and on what grounds the case moved through the national system.
serbian-court-decisions.purpose: To keep the Serbian courtroom record in one readable sequence.

asylum.title: Asylum track
asylum.subtitle: Protection proceedings that ran alongside extradition and addressed the risk side of the case.
asylum.contains: Asylum decisions, appeals, and related documents from the international-protection process.
asylum.proves: That the risk of persecution and ill-treatment was examined not only in extradition proceedings but also in a separate protective framework.
asylum.purpose: To show the parallel protection route that mattered for the surrender risk assessment.

appeals-to-serbian-authorities.title: Petitions to Serbian authorities
appeals-to-serbian-authorities.subtitle: The non-judicial advocacy track inside Serbia.
appeals-to-serbian-authorities.contains: Letters to the Minister of Justice, the Ombudsman, the presidential administration, and other Serbian authorities, plus replies and acknowledgements.
appeals-to-serbian-authorities.proves: That the defence sought intervention not only through courts but also through executive and constitutional channels.
appeals-to-serbian-authorities.purpose: To gather the Serbian administrative and civic advocacy record in one place.

international-support.title: International and political support
international-support.subtitle: The outward-facing advocacy work around the case.
international-support.contains: Submissions to UNHCR, the EU Delegation, and Serbian political parties.
international-support.proves: That the risks raised by the case were framed internationally as a human-rights concern rather than a narrow procedural dispute.
international-support.purpose: To document the broader support and pressure surrounding the Serbian proceedings.

extradition-serbia.contains: The extradition request, the charge package, Serbian court decisions, asylum materials, and submissions to Serbian and international actors.
extradition-serbia.proves: That the extradition case relied on the same disputed Russian materials while running alongside arguments about risk, fairness, and ECHR violations.
extradition-serbia.purpose: To present the full Serbian extradition record without separating the courtroom story from the protection story.

interpol.title: Interpol
interpol.subtitle: A separate track dealing with the Red Notice and the filing before the Commission for the Control of Interpol’s Files.
interpol.contains: The CCF complaint, follow-up materials, and the Commission’s response on the Red Notice issue.
interpol.proves: That the international wanted notice was challenged through Interpol’s own review mechanism, apart from the Serbian court process.
interpol.purpose: To show the dedicated international remedy used against the notice itself.

core-evidence.title: Core merits evidence
core-evidence.subtitle: This section is organised by evidentiary meaning rather than by addressee: the deal itself, the court record around it, Lagovskii’s role, and the investigators’ reinterpretation of those materials.

investigative-materials.title: Investigative materials and commentary
investigative-materials.subtitle: The documents through which investigators tried to turn the transaction into a criminal narrative.
investigative-materials.contains: The inspection protocol, references to the so-called real value, and the defence commentary on those materials.
investigative-materials.proves: How investigators recast commercial documents as signs of a criminal scheme.
investigative-materials.purpose: To expose the weak points of the prosecution theory using the investigators’ own file.

deal-court-decisions.title: Court decisions on the transaction
deal-court-decisions.subtitle: The arbitration record concerning the land transaction, including a translation for non-Russian readers.
deal-court-decisions.contains: Decisions and rulings in case A41-20164/2022, including the translation of the key arbitration ruling.
deal-court-decisions.proves: That the dispute was already tested in civil proceedings and the court record does not support a theft narrative.
deal-court-decisions.purpose: To provide the judicial baseline from which the accusation should be assessed.

deal-documents-and-acts.title: Transaction documents and corporate acts
deal-documents-and-acts.subtitle: The primary paperwork of the deal itself and the internal acts tied to it.
deal-documents-and-acts.contains: The sale agreement, Protocol No. 58, and the documents directly governing how the transaction was documented.
deal-documents-and-acts.proves: How the deal was actually structured on paper, before any investigative interpretation was layered onto it.
deal-documents-and-acts.purpose: To let readers see the primary record in its own terms.

professional-status-and-work.title: Professional status and legal work
professional-status-and-work.subtitle: Documents clarifying Lagovskii’s role as an outside professional rather than a company executive.
professional-status-and-work.contains: The legal-services agreement and the sole-proprietor registry extract confirming his professional standing.
professional-status-and-work.proves: That Lagovskii acted as an external lawyer and entrepreneur, not as someone managing the asset on the company’s behalf.
professional-status-and-work.purpose: To correct one of the central role reversals built into the accusation.

core-evidence.contains: Arbitration decisions, transaction documents, records proving professional status, and investigative materials built on top of those documents.
core-evidence.proves: That the underlying dispute was commercial and civil in nature, while the criminal narrative depends on re-reading existing paperwork through a prosecutorial lens.
core-evidence.purpose: To give readers fast access to the core documents that matter for the merits of the accusation.

salikov-abuse.title: Report on Salikov's abuse of power
salikov-abuse.desc: Application concerning crimes related to abuse of authority and falsification.

crime-report-salikov.title: Crime report against Salikov
crime-report-salikov.desc: Report of a crime committed by Salikov, filed with investigative authorities.

witness-testimony-check.title: Application for testimony verification
witness-testimony-check.desc: Demand to verify knowingly false statements by prosecution witnesses.

obvinenie.title: Charge
obvinenie.desc: Fraud charge under Art. 159(4) RF Criminal Code (organised-group fraud on a particularly large scale). Drawn up in absentia without notifying the accused; contradicted by final arbitration rulings.

obvinenie-serbian.title: Charge - Serbian version
obvinenie-serbian.desc: Version of the indictment submitted to Serbian judicial authorities for substantive consideration as part of the extradition request.

obvinenie-errors-final.title: Defence commentary on the indictment
obvinenie-errors-final.desc: Page-by-page defence analysis of the indictment: factual errors, internal contradictions, conflicts with final arbitration rulings, and procedural defects, all undermining the charge.

international-search-warrant.title: International wanted notice (Red Notice basis)
international-search-warrant.desc: Order declaring an international wanted notice — the basis for the Interpol Red Notice request. Issued one month after the in-absentia arrest of 27 Dec 2024.

international-search-warrant-serbian.title: International wanted notice — Serbian file
international-search-warrant-serbian.desc: Translation/version of the international wanted order submitted to Serbian authorities as part of the extradition file, accompanying the Russian-language original.

search-warrant.title: Domestic wanted order
search-warrant.desc: Domestic wanted order issued on 27 Dec 2024 despite the investigation's knowledge of the applicant's residence in Serbia — violates Art. 210 of the RF Code of Criminal Procedure.

search-warrant-serbian.title: Domestic wanted order — Serbian file
search-warrant-serbian.desc: Version of the domestic wanted order transmitted to Serbian authorities for use in the extradition proceedings.

arrest-warrant.title: Arrest warrant (in absentia)
arrest-warrant.desc: In-absentia arrest warrant issued by Tverskoy District Court, Moscow, on 27 Dec 2024 without notice to or participation of the accused.

arrest-warrant-serbian.title: Arrest warrant — Serbian file
arrest-warrant-serbian.desc: Copy of the arrest warrant transmitted to Serbian judicial authorities for use in the extradition procedure.

genprokuratura-request.title: Russian Prosecutor General extradition request
genprokuratura-request.desc: Formal extradition request from the Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation to the competent authorities of the Republic of Serbia — the central procedural document of the extradition case.

genprokuratura-request-serbian.title: Prosecutor General request — Serbian file
genprokuratura-request-serbian.desc: Serbian-language version of the Prosecutor General's extradition request, used directly in the Serbian court proceedings.

supreme-court-decision.title: Serbian Supreme Court decision (11 Feb 2026)
supreme-court-decision.desc: On 11 Feb 2026 the Serbian Supreme Court unanimously rejected the extraordinary petition for the protection of legality. Substantive defence arguments were not examined, formally exhausting all domestic remedies.

higher-court-decision.title: Higher Court decision
higher-court-decision.desc: Higher Court of Serbia decision of 4 July 2025 in the extradition case — reflects the initial level of judicial review within the national extradition procedure.

appeal-filing.title: Appeal against the extradition decision
appeal-filing.desc: Appeal against the extradition decision filed on 07 Dec 2025 within the national judicial track. Sets out ECHR arguments and violations of international extradition standards.

minister-appeal-ru.title: Appeal to the Serbian Minister of Justice (Russian version)
minister-appeal-ru.desc: Russian version of the appeal to the Serbian Minister of Justice: detailed arguments under the ECHR on lack of fair trial in Russia and risk to the applicant's life and health, requesting refusal of extradition.

minister-appeal-sr.title: Appeal to the Serbian Minister of Justice (Serbian version)
minister-appeal-sr.desc: Serbian version of the appeal to the Ministry of Justice — submitted simultaneously with the Russian version and addressed directly to Serbian officials for substantive review.

personal-letter-berisha.title: Personal appeal to Minister Dema Berisha
personal-letter-berisha.desc: Personal letter to Minister for Human and Minority Rights Dema Berisha requesting intervention on human-rights grounds ahead of the extradition decision.

ombudsman-appeal-ru.title: Appeal to the Serbian Ombudsman (Russian version)
ombudsman-appeal-ru.desc: Russian version of the Ombudsman complaint: detailed description of violations of the right to a fair trial and procedural guarantees in the Serbian extradition proceedings.

ombudsman-appeal-sr.title: Appeal to the Serbian Ombudsman (Serbian version)
ombudsman-appeal-sr.desc: Serbian version of the Ombudsman complaint — filed alongside the Russian version for direct review by the competent institution.

ombudsman-complaint-may-2026.title: Complaint to the Ombudsman (May 2026)
ombudsman-complaint-may-2026.desc: Additional complaint to the Serbian Ombudsman filed in May 2026 after successive asylum rejections and the exhaustion of the national extradition track.

ombudsman-response.title: Reply from the Serbian Ombudsman
ombudsman-response.desc: Official reply dated 06 Jun 2025 from the Serbian Ombudsman to the complaint concerning procedural violations in the extradition proceedings.

UNHCR-letter.title: Letter to UNHCR (21 Apr 2026)
UNHCR-letter.desc: Submission to the UNHCR describing risks of extradition to Russia — torture, politically motivated prosecution, absence of a fair trial — and the lack of effective domestic protection. Sent 21 Apr 2026.

ministry-receipt.title: Confirmation of receipt by the Serbian Ministry of Justice
ministry-receipt.desc: Formal acknowledgement by the Serbian Ministry of Justice of receipt of the defence submission dated 27 May 2025. Evidences proper notification of the competent authority.

vucic-admin-response.title: Response from the Office of the President of Serbia (19 May 2026)
vucic-admin-response.desc: Response from the General Secretariat of the President: the appeal was forwarded to the Ministry of Justice of Serbia without substantive consideration — 19 May 2026.

vucic-letter.title: Letter to President Aleksandar Vučić
vucic-letter.desc: Direct appeal to Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić requesting personal intervention to prevent extradition given unrefuted evidence of political motivation in the Russian prosecution.

eurointegration-ministry-letter.title: Submission to the Ministry for European Integration
eurointegration-ministry-letter.desc: Submission to the Serbian Ministry for European Integration arguing that extradition would contradict rule-of-law standards and Serbia's commitments under its EU accession obligations.

lagovskii-dmitrii-asylum-decision.title: Asylum Office decision (23 Feb 2026)
lagovskii-dmitrii-asylum-decision.desc: First-instance refusal of asylum and subsidiary protection issued by the Serbian Asylum Office on 23 Feb 2026 — without adequate assessment of real risks on return to Russia.

asylum-commission-decision.title: Asylum Commission decision (23 Mar 2026)
asylum-commission-decision.desc: Asylum Commission of Serbia rejected the appeal on 23 Mar 2026. The only remaining avenue is the Serbian Administrative Court, where the case is currently pending.

zeleni-front-letter.title: Letter to Zeleni Front
zeleni-front-letter.desc: Appeal to the Serbian civil-society organisation Zeleni Front asking for public support and advocacy to raise awareness about the human-rights dimension of the case.

ssp-letter.title: Letter to the SSP party
ssp-letter.desc: Letter to the Party of Freedom and Justice (SSP) outlining the case and requesting the party to take a public stance against what amounts to a politically motivated extradition.

nps-letter.title: Letter to the NPS party
nps-letter.desc: Letter to the People's Movement of Serbia (NPS) describing the case and asking the party to use parliamentary and public tools to oppose the extradition.

eu-delegation-letter.title: Letter to the EU Delegation in Serbia
eu-delegation-letter.desc: Appeal to the EU Delegation in Serbia and the European Commission requesting diplomatic pressure to prevent an extradition that violates European human-rights standards. Sent 20 Apr 2026.

apellyatsiya-mosgorsud.title: Appellate ruling of Moscow City Court
apellyatsiya-mosgorsud.desc: Appellate ruling of Moscow City Court in the criminal case — records the position of the second-instance court and the procedural history on appeal.

prigovor-achkasovu.title: Verdict against Achkasov et al.
prigovor-achkasovu.desc: Guilty verdict against co-defendants in the case, used by the investigation as prejudice against Lagovskiy D.V. The verdict does not establish facts binding on the extradition proceedings.

case-A41-20164-2022-20250512.title: Determination (12 May 2025)
case-A41-20164-2022-20250512.desc: Closing determination in case A41-20164/2022, issued 12 May 2025 — formally concludes the arbitration proceedings.

case-A41-20164-2022-20250124.title: Cassation ruling (24 Jan 2025)
case-A41-20164-2022-20250124.desc: Moscow District Arbitrazh Court rejected the cassation appeal on 24 Jan 2025, upholding the finding that the FEZ JSC land-sale transaction was lawful.

case-A41-20164-2022-20240913.title: Appellate ruling (13 Sep 2024)
case-A41-20164-2022-20240913.desc: 10th Arbitrazh Appellate Court upheld the first-instance ruling on 13 Sep 2024: the land sale was lawful and no shareholder loss was proved.

case-A41-20164-2022-20240627.title: Moscow Region Arbitrazh Court (27 Jun 2024)
case-A41-20164-2022-20240627.desc: Moscow Region Arbitrazh Court ruled on 27 Jun 2024 that the FEZ JSC land sale was fully lawful and that no shareholder loss had occurred — directly refuting the fraud charge.

arbitration-decision-translation.title: Arbitration ruling — certified translation
arbitration-decision-translation.desc: Certified Serbian-language translation of the 27 Jun 2024 arbitration ruling — submitted to Serbian courts as part of the extradition defence file.

email-khrabrykh-to-interpol-ccf.title: Defence reply to Interpol CCF (28 Nov 2025)
email-khrabrykh-to-interpol-ccf.desc: Letter from defence lawyer Khrabrykh S.V. to the Interpol Commission for the Control of Files (CCF) with supporting exhibits proving the applicant had no managerial authority — the key argument for challenging the Red Notice.

interpol-ccf-response-red-notice.title: Interpol CCF letter - complaint registered
interpol-ccf-response-red-notice.desc: Interpol CCF confirms registration of the complaint against the Red Notice (case CCF/135/R1610.25) and commencement of a review for compliance with Interpol's rules. Dated 28 Oct 2025.

mosgorsud-2025-10-16.title: Moscow City Court: reply on Article 125 complaint
mosgorsud-2025-10-16.desc: Reply of the Moscow City Court stating that the Article 125 complaint was returned, without giving substantive protection on the merits.

mosgorsud-rozysk-refusal.title: Moscow City Court: no answer because of wanted status
mosgorsud-rozysk-refusal.desc: The court relies on formal defects and wanted status as grounds not to review the complaint on the merits.

tver-access-refusal.title: Tverskoy Court: denial of access to justice
tver-access-refusal.desc: Document from the Tverskoy Court confirming denial of effective judicial protection in complaints tied to the criminal prosecution.

kassatsiya-refusal.title: Cassation refusal
kassatsiya-refusal.desc: Cassation-level refusal continuing the same pattern: no merits review.

tver-complaint-refusal-1.title: Tverskoy Court: refusal to accept complaint
tver-complaint-refusal-1.desc: First refusal by the Tverskoy Court to accept the complaint for consideration.

tver-complaint-refusal-2.title: Tverskoy Court: repeated refusal to accept complaint
tver-complaint-refusal-2.desc: Repeated refusal to accept a comparable complaint, confirming the systematic nature of the block.

shchelkovo-return-order.title: Shchelkovo Court: order returning Article 125 complaint
shchelkovo-return-order.desc: Order of 20 June 2025 returning the complaint against IC RF inaction instead of hearing it on the merits.

shchelkovo-response-697.title: Shchelkovo Court: reply No. 697/2025
shchelkovo-response-697.desc: Court letter stating that the Article 125 complaint was returned. This is notice of procedural dead-end, not judicial protection.

mitrokhina-otvety.title: Mitrokhina: all responses
mitrokhina-otvety.desc: Combined PDF with template replies from the Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office, best illustrating the systematic refusal to engage with the merits.

mitrokhina-response-13.title: Mitrokhina: response No. 13
mitrokhina-response-13.desc: Formal response from the Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office with no substantive review of the unlawful prosecution arguments.

mitrokhina-response-31.title: Mitrokhina: response No. 31 forwarding back to MVD investigators
mitrokhina-response-31.desc: Reply effectively sending the complaint back to the same investigative bloc being challenged.

prokuror-mo-response.title: Response from the Moscow Region Prosecutor
prokuror-mo-response.desc: Regional prosecutor's response to the complaint received from the GPO, again without independent assessment of the defence arguments.

prokopenko-otvety.title: Prokopenko: General Prosecutor responses
prokopenko-otvety.desc: Official responses of 17 March 2026 treating the complaints formally, without legal analysis of the core defence arguments.

genprok-ogr-154993-response.title: GPO response on complaint OGR-154993-26
genprok-ogr-154993-response.desc: General Prosecutor's Office reply rejecting any further review and treating the allegations as already checked.

prokuratura-no-reply-response.title: Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office: reply on “non-receipt of responses”
prokuratura-no-reply-response.desc: Reply explaining that earlier applications were supposedly already processed, instead of resolving the underlying complaint.

mitrokhina-forward-to-gsu-2026-04-20.title: Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office: forwarding complaint against Mitrokhina to GSU
mitrokhina-forward-to-gsu-2026-04-20.desc: Cover letter of 20 April 2026 sending the complaint back to the same investigative bloc instead of addressing it on the merits.

mitrokhina-response-2026-04-23.title: Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office: Mitrokhina response of 23 April 2026
mitrokhina-response-2026-04-23.desc: Response adopting the investigative narrative and giving no independent assessment of the applicant's arguments.

kuznetsov-forward-to-gsu.title: Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office: forwarding complaint against Kuznetsov to GSU
kuznetsov-forward-to-gsu.desc: Formal forwarding of a complaint about departmental inaction back into the MVD system being challenged.

prokuratura-mo-response-16-4-469-2025.title: Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office: reply No. 16/4-469-2025
prokuratura-mo-response-16-4-469-2025.desc: Regional prosecutor's reply again reducing the complaint to a template confirmation of the investigators' position.

mitrokhina-all-responses-bundle.title: Mitrokhina responses — consolidated bundle
mitrokhina-all-responses-bundle.desc: A compiled file containing the Moscow Region Prosecutor's formal replies to complaints about the unlawful prosecution. It is useful here because it shows the repeated template language and the absence of any substantive review.

chugunkov-response-660170.title: Chugunkov: reply No. 3/267704660170
chugunkov-response-660170.desc: Template MVD reply to the report of Salikov's crimes, without addressing the allegations on the merits.

chugunkov-response-751007.title: Chugunkov: reply No. 3/267704751007
chugunkov-response-751007.desc: Second identical reply from the same date, again without analysis of the specific facts raised.

kuznetsov-response-2025-06-25.title: Kuznetsov: reply of 25 June 2025
kuznetsov-response-2025-06-25.desc: One of a series of near-identical GSU MVD replies to complaints about procedural violations and inaction.

kuznetsov-response-2025-07-20.title: Kuznetsov: reply of 20 July 2025
kuznetsov-response-2025-07-20.desc: Repeat template reply on criminal case No. 42401460225000036, with no merits analysis.

kuznetsov-response-2025-08-01.title: Kuznetsov: reply of 1 August 2025
kuznetsov-response-2025-08-01.desc: Another identical GSU MVD response confirming the systematic nature of the non-substantive review.

kuznetsov-reply-2025-07-14.title: Kuznetsov: reply of 14 July 2025
kuznetsov-reply-2025-07-14.desc: Reply from E.I. Kuznetsov, Head of 6th Section, dated 14 July 2025. The fourth in the series. Contains the standard refusal formula without engaging with the substance of the arguments.

kuznetsov-response-2025-08-14.title: Kuznetsov: reply of 14 August 2025
kuznetsov-response-2025-08-14.desc: The next reply in the same series: allegations of fabrication and investigative inaction again go unanswered on the merits.

kuznetsov-response-2025-08-20.title: Kuznetsov: reply of 20 August 2025
kuznetsov-response-2025-08-20.desc: Another boilerplate GSU MVD response showing that complaints were logged but not substantively reviewed.

kuznetsov-response-2025-09-01.title: Kuznetsov: reply of 1 September 2025
kuznetsov-response-2025-09-01.desc: Yet another formal reply with no fresh legal analysis, part of a long chain of repetitive refusals.

upch-response-1.title: Ombudsman reply forwarding to Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office
